h1: From Concrete to Playgrounds: How Indian Cities Can Create More Child-Friendly Spaces

props.title: From Concrete to Playgrounds: How Indian Cities Can Create More Child-Friendly Spaces
props.summaryText: From unused plots to rooftops and school grounds after hours: practical ways cities, builders and residents can turn concrete into places for children to play.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Children on swings at an outdoor playground

takeaways.text: Child-friendly cities need many small play spaces close to homes, not only a few big parks.
Unused plots, rooftops, school grounds and street spaces can all become play spaces.
Play along everyday routes, such as near bus stops, markets and schools, reaches more children.
Resident groups and builders can act on their own land without waiting for a city plan.

faq.q: How can Indian cities create more child-friendly spaces?
faq.a: By creating small play spaces close to homes on unused plots and rooftops, opening school grounds after hours, adding play elements along everyday routes, closing streets for play at set times, and making parks safe and accessible.
A street that is closed to traffic at set times, such as Sunday mornings, so children and families can play, cycle and meet safely. Several Indian cities have run play street events.

faq.q: What can a housing society do to create more play space?
faq.a: Use podiums, terraces and underused corners for play, add play panels on walls, combine play with seating and an outdoor gym, and keep existing play areas well maintained.
